sentences.sentence: The NHS says most sore throats are caused by viruses such as colds or flu, and bacteria are a less common cause.

sentences.sentence: Laryngitis, tonsillitis, strep throat and glandular fever can also cause a sore throat, and so can smoking.

sentences.sentence: NICE says that in older children and adults, pus on the tonsils, painful glands in the neck and a fever without a cough point more towards a bacterial infection.

sentences.sentence: A sore throat usually clears up on its own and often lasts about a week.

sentences.sentence: Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help with pain and fever, although not everyone can take ibuprofen safely, so a pharmacist can advise.

sentences.sentence: Drinking fluids and resting are also advised.

sentences.sentence: NICE says most people with a sore throat will not need an antibiotic.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says antibiotics are prescribed only if the GP thinks a bacterial infection is likely.

sentences.sentence: Tonsillitis commonly causes a sore throat, trouble swallowing, fever, earache and tender swollen glands in the neck.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A GP can usually diagnose tonsillitis from the symptoms and a look at the throat, and may arrange a swab or a glandular fever blood test if symptoms are severe or persistent.

sentences.sentence: Glandular fever can cause a high temperature, swollen glands, a sore throat, rash, headache and tiredness, and the NHS says it is most common in people aged 15 to 24.

sentences.sentence: Antibiotics do not work for glandular fever because it is caused by a virus.

sentences.sentence: Quinsy is a collection of pus between the tonsil and the wall of the throat, and is a rare complication of tonsillitis.

sentences.sentence: Sources agree on seeking advice from a GP if the sore throat has not improved after a week, if there is a high temperature or the person feels hot and shivery, or if the immune system is weakened or a medicine could be causing the sore throat.

sentences.sentence: A sore throat that does not get better within 10 to 14 days, or that gets worse rather than better, may suggest glandular fever.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E for struggling to breathe, being unable to swallow even with pain relief, or drooling or spitting out saliva because swallowing is too painful.
